h: Capability Brown Parkland and City Treasures
p: The parkland at Temple Newsam was landscaped by Capability Brown, the famous eighteenth-century garden designer, and you can still see his work in the rolling grassland, the lakes and the carefully placed clumps of trees. It's a lovely setting for a long walk after your session, and in late spring the gardens put on a beautiful show.

Leeds has some brilliant follow-ups too. The Royal Armouries Museum at Leeds Dock holds the national collection of arms and armour, with displays that captivate kids and adults alike. Kirkstall Abbey, on the west side of the city, is a remarkably well-preserved Cistercian abbey ruin and a peaceful place to explore. Roundhay Park is another huge green space, and its Tropical World is great on a rainy day.
Leeds Industrial Museum at Armley Mills tells the story of the city's woollen mills, which ties in nicely with the industrial heritage of West Yorkshire.

As for the treetops, allow a couple of hours, and remember that parking on busy days can take a while. Aim to arrive a little early for your briefing. Bring water, and a snack for afterwards, as you'll likely want to spend the rest of the day exploring the estate.
If you've got a mixed group, the farm and gardens are ideal for those who'd rather stay on the ground.
